why:
I checked the PASS and FAIL conditions of all seven verifier checks against the words of their expect lines.

- **Checks 1–5:** each requires the exact stdout plus one trailing newline. Check 1 also requires "exit status is 0". Each expect line says this.
- **Check 3:** "including rows missing or out of order" follows from "exactly".
- **Check 5:** the two-character JSON escape matches the literal JSON in the expect line.
- **Check 6:** the conditions match the words: npm test exits 0, and at least one test runs bin/csv2json.js with `--tsv`, feeds it input containing tabs, and asserts on the output.
- **Check 7:** it requires only that README mentions `--tsv` and gives "an example invocation that uses it".

The stricter items are all under "Advisory (none of this affects PASS or FAIL)". These are saying the flag means tab-separated input, the flag working in any argument position, the `test:cli` note, and changes outside the non-goals. No check adds an exact-wording, mutation or branch rule to its PASS or FAIL conditions.
